implementation_notes: Swift enums are algebraic: each case may carry a tuple of associated values of its own types, switch destructures them and the compiler requires exhaustive coverage without a default, and payload-free cases share the same syntax. Recursive variants are declared indirect (or indirect case) so the compiler inserts the indirection; Optional is itself an enum, there being no null. For wire formats the Codable synthesis encodes the case as a tagged structure, which keeps the serialised form and the union in step.
pitfalls: A case with associated values cannot be compared with == unless every associated type is Equatable (equality is synthesised only then); without it, matching on payload values needs explicit pattern guards.
A case name is also a constructor function, so .circle can be stored or passed as a closure - convenient, but the resulting reference holds no payload and cannot be switched as a value.
For resilient (library-evolution) public enums, @frozen is required before clients may switch exhaustively; a non-frozen enum forces a @unknown default and re-opens the set at run time.
Recursive cases must be marked indirect or the compiler rejects the type for infinite size; the indirection also means heap allocation for deep trees.
